content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in TypeScript: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `main.ts`. Build and run it with Deno — `deno run`, `deno check` and `deno test`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. --- total 16 drwxr-xr-x 4 vshynkarenko staff 128 11 Okt. 13:38 . drwxr-xr-x 4 vshynkarenko staff 128 11 Okt. 13:38 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1861 11 Okt. 13:38 BRIEF.md -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1279 13 Sep. 17:41 main.ts

content.text:
I extended `main.ts` with all four additions. It type-checks with `deno check`, the original three commands produce byte-identical output to the old version on a sample script, and the new commands behave as the brief specifies in my tests. **What changed** - **`prio

`**: sets priority (new tasks default to 5). An unknown id writes `no such task `. A `p` that is not a single digit writes `bad priority

` and changes nothing. - **`list`**: open tasks sorted by priority ascending, then id. The line format is unchanged. - **`list all`**: every task in the same order, as `- ` or `x <id> <title>`. - **Unknown first word**: writes `? <word>`. **Choices I made where the brief was silent** - For `prio`, I check the id before the priority, so `prio 9 10` on a missing task reports `no such task 9`. - Missing arguments are treated as bad input: `prio` alone gives `no such task 0`, and `prio 1` with no digit gives `bad priority ` (empty). This matches how `done` already handles a bad id. - Extra tokens after `prio <id> <p>` are ignored. - Only the exact argument `all` triggers the full listing. `list` with any other argument behaves as before. - Whitespace-only lines are now treated as blank and skipped. Before, they were silently ignored. **Behaviour you may want to review** - A line with leading whitespace, such as ` add x`, now prints `? ` with an empty word, since the first word is empty. It was silently ignored before. - A CRLF file would now print `? list\r` for each command, where it was silently ignored before. I did not add CRLF handling because the brief does not mention it. My test inputs and the original copy are in `/tmp/trackertest` and `/tmp/main.orig.ts`, outside the project directory. The project still contains only `BRIEF.md` and `main.ts`.
